result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): B is the better answer because it says what the quarter will not deliver (no full redesign or big-bang rewrite), names onboarding as a benefit, and suggests cheap ways to get a rough number before the quarter starts. A invents no numbers and its plan is slightly tighter, but it never says what is out of scope. Both run well past a page, and B's '10% of front-end time' example comes close to suggesting a made-up figure. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): B fits the brief better. It ties the benefits to web and app across three squads in concrete terms (promos, checkout, fixing the same bug in several places). It refuses to invent an estimate, and it lays out a month-by-month plan with a baseline first, then an end-of-quarter decision to continue, scale or stop. A says what is out of scope more clearly ('no full redesign'), but it adds an example figure ('about 10% of front-end time') that a speaker could easily repeat as fact. Both answers take 'a quarter' to mean 25% of two people's time rather than three months, and both run longer than a page.
